activity.notes: Kavad I (also written Kawad I, Kavadh I, and scholarly Kawād I) first ruled the Sasanian Empire from 488 until his deposition in 496. Encyclopaedia Iranica treats his reign as a turning point in Sasanian history and explicitly separates a first reign of 488-496 from his later restoration. ATLAS therefore ends this rules Activity in 496 and does not project Kavad's authority through the interruption, during which Zamasp/Jamasp occupied the throne. His later restored reign is represented by a separate Activity for the same Person and Polity rather than by duplicating the Person or fabricating continuous rule.

sources.title: KAWĀD I i. Reign — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica identifies Kavad's reign as a turning point in Sasanian history, labels the first reign 488-496, and describes his deposition and subsequent escape to the Hephthalite court.

sources.title: Chronology of Iranian History Part 1 — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: The Iranica chronology records Kavad's accession in 488 and his deposition by Jamasp in 496, supporting the year-level boundaries of the first reign.
